title: The Morning Brief: CFP adds mid-major voice; Dolphins shift power; FIFA blackmail claims widen
dek: College football's playoff committee gains a 12-year mid-major AD; Miami's power structure centralizes under a new CEO; and Jordan's football federation accuses FIFA of withholding prize money to coerce endorsement of Gianni Infantino's re-election.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Three governance shifts reshape power structures across college football, the NFL, and international soccer, each consolidating authority or exposing leverage tactics at moments of institutional vulnerability.
bottom_line: Three institutions reshaped their power structures or faced transparency crises on the same morning: the CFP added mid-major representation, the Dolphins centralized authority under family leadership, and FIFA faced direct allegations of financial coercion to secure an endorsement. The honest read is that each move tests whether governance can remain legitimate under new arrangements. What to watch: whether Gillin's appointment signals genuine mid-major voice in playoff ranking; whether Sillman's tenure produces different hiring or strategy decisions at Miami; whether other federation leaders corroborate FIFA's pressure tactics before the November 18 deadline for presidential candidates; whether Reusser's narrow lead survives the mountains; and how the Pac-12 competes this fall despite the settlement's undisclosed terms.
body: The morning's news centers on three separate but thematically linked changes in how sports organizations make decisions and wield power: the addition of mid-major representation to the College Football Playoff selection committee, a family succession move that consolidates control at the Miami Dolphins, and an escalating corruption allegation against FIFA that expands beyond Europe into Asian federation leadership.

Appalachian State athletics director Doug Gillin has been appointed to the CFP selection committee, replacing Louisiana's Bryan Maggard, who moved to Missouri. Gillin brings 12 years of mid-major leadership to a group that ranks the top 25 teams and selects the 12-team playoff field. His tenure at App State included oversight of multiple conference championships and a 2019 finish at No. 20 in the final CFP rankings. The appointment marks a visible nod to mid-major voices in playoff selection, though the scope and duration of Gillin's role remain unannounced.

The Dolphins have named Daniel Sillman, 37, as CEO of Ross Sports & Entertainment, elevating the son-in-law of owner Stephen Ross to operational control of the franchise and signaling a family succession plan for the sports portfolio. Sillman, who co-founded Relevent Sports, now oversees head coach Jeff Hafley, GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, and other football leadership reporting directly to him. Tom Garfinkel, who served as team president for 13 years, is stepping down but will remain as vice chairman. The move consolidates authority over both football operations and business decisions under a single executive after a 13-year period of separate presidential and operational leadership.

International soccer's governance crisis deepened when Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, president of Jordan's national football federation and a former FIFA vice president, accused FIFA of withholding $4.2 million in prize money owed to his country as financial leverage to secure his endorsement of Gianni Infantino's re-election. According to the desk's reporting, Prince Ali stated that FIFA verbally communicated during the World Cup that endorsing Infantino would help Jordan resolve outstanding financial matters, after refusing assistance for months prior. The allegation represents the first time a sitting member federation has accused FIFA of explicit financial coercion tied to Infantino's presidency, expanding a widening corruption scandal beyond the European and North American criticism the organization has already faced over Infantino's failed World Cup investment scheme.

In cycling, Marlen Reusser of Switzerland won stage four of the Tour de France Femmes, a 21-kilometer individual time trial from Gevrey-Chambertin to Dijon completed in 27 minutes, 30 seconds. The world time trial champion assumed the yellow jersey with a 14-second lead over defending champion Demi Vollering, with five stages remaining before the Mont Ventoux finish. The victory positions Reusser as race leader entering the mountains, where lighter climbers often pressure time trial specialists.

Joseph Parker's provisional suspension for testing positive for cocaine has been lifted, clearing the 34-year-old former WBO heavyweight champion to compete again. The test came on October 25, the same day Parker fought Fabio Wardley at London's O2 Arena. Investigations by UK Anti-Doping and the British Boxing Board of Control remain open, and a potential ban of up to two years is still possible. Parker has denied knowingly taking any banned substances.

NBC Sports has secured a multi-year renewal of Preakness Stakes broadcast rights, fending off bids from Fox Sports, Netflix, and Amazon. The network has held Preakness rights since 2001. The renewal follows improved viewership in May 2026, when the race drew 5.5 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, the largest audience since 2021 and a 22 percent increase from 4.9 million viewers in 2025.

The Pac-12 and Mountain West conferences reached final settlement agreements resolving all pending litigation over conference realignment, exit fees, and a disputed poaching clause. The deal concludes disputes involving Boise State, Colorado State, Utah State, San Diego State, and Fresno State, each of which left the Mountain West for the Pac-12. The litigation centered on the validity of a $55 million penalty structure tied to a poaching clause in the Mountain West's original scheduling agreement. The exact terms of the settlement remain undisclosed.

Tour de France Femmes organizers have implemented pre-race equipment checks to prevent riders from using bra padding and other aerodynamic modifications. Research cited by the desk's reporting suggests padding in bras can produce one-second-per-kilometre gains in aerodynamic efficiency. Race organiser ASO issued a statement citing UCI regulations prohibiting non-essential clothing that could modify riders' morphology, with checks taking place 10 minutes before each rider's start time.
